title: Binary kagome superconducting candidates hosting topological electronic states
authors: Xin-Wei Yi, Jing-Yang You, Gang Su
abstract: Topological superconductivity has attracted broad interest because of its connection to Majorana fermions and quantum computation. Kagome materials provide a natural setting in which interesting electronic structures, topological surface states, and superconductivity may occur in nearby energy windows. Here we carry out a systematic first-principles search for binary kagome superconducting candidates with topological electronic states across several structural families $A_mB_n$ ($m$:$n$=3:1; 3:2; 1:1). The screening combines formation-energy and phonon-stability filtering, magnetic-ground-state searches, electron-phonon-coupling calculations, and topological electronic-structure analysis. We identify 286 nonmagnetic dynamically stable candidates for electron-phonon-coupling analysis, among which 84 have estimated transition temperatures above 3 K and seven exceed the $\sim 9$ K reference scale of existing ambient-pressure kagome superconductors. In addition, several systems are predicted to host abundant topological surface states near the Fermi level. NbBi is identified as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological metal with clear Dirac-cone topological surface states and a kagome-derived flat band near $E_F$. Ti$_3$Si, with the largest estimated $T_\text{c}=15.2$ K in this dataset, shows nodal-line-derived drumhead surface states and selected nodes that survive spin-orbit coupling near $E_F$. Combining superconductivity with nontrivial topological electronic structures, the binary kagome compounds predicted here represent compact and chemically tunable candidate platforms for topological superconductivity and for exploring kagome-related quantum phenomena.
summary: This work presents a comprehensive computational search for novel binary kagome superconductors that possess intrinsic topological electronic states. By combining stability filtering, electron-phonon coupling calculations, and topological analysis, the authors predict several high-$T_c$ candidates, notably $	ext{Ti}_3	ext{Si}$, making these materials promising platforms for topological superconductivity.
main_problem: The paper systematically searches for binary kagome superconducting candidates that simultaneously host topological electronic states, aiming for materials exhibiting topological superconductivity.
main_result: They identified 286 stable candidates, with seven exceeding the ambient-pressure reference $T_c$ of $\sim 9$ K. Specifically, $	ext{Ti}_3	ext{Si}$ was found with the highest estimated $T_c$ of $15.2$ K.
method: The study employs a high-throughput first-principles workflow combining phonon stability checks, magnetic ground-state searches, electron-phonon coupling (EPC) calculations, and topological electronic structure analysis.
model_or_system: The focus is on binary compounds forming kagome lattices within structural prototypes $A_mB_n$ ($m:n=3:1$, $3:2$, $1:1$). The theoretical framework models superconductivity via EPC and topological properties using $\mathbb{Z}_2$ indices.
key_observables: Estimated superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), electron-phonon coupling constant ($\lambda$), topological indices ($\mathbb{Z}_2$), and surface state characteristics (e.g., Dirac cones).
important_parameters: The search filters include formation energy and phonon stability. High $T_c$ candidates are those with strong EPC and topological features.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on first-principles calculations and approximations such as the McMillan/Allen–Dynes formulas for $T_c$ estimation and the isotropic EPC approximation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows prototype crystal structures. Figure 2 plots $T_c$ vs. $\lambda$ and details phonon dispersions/EPC spectral functions for representative systems. Figure 3 details the electronic topology of $	ext{NbBi}$.
paper_structure: The paper follows a systematic search methodology: first, filtering for stable candidates; second, calculating EPC and estimating $T_c$; and finally, analyzing the topological electronic structure of the promising superconducting materials.
why_interesting: The combination of superconductivity (a many-body phenomenon) with intrinsic topological order in a highly structured lattice like kagome is central to realizing exotic quantum states, which is a key area of condensed matter theory.

The A atoms (gold) form kagome layers (K), while the B atoms (grey) form hon- eycomb layers (H). (b–e) Crystal structures of four prototype fami- lies: (b) A3B (P63/mmc), (c) A3B (Pm¯3m), (d) AB (P6/mmm), and (e) A3B2 (R¯3m). These structures can be generated by stacking kagome and honeycomb layers in different sequences and registries. The drawings highlight the in-plane shifts between adjacent layers.

FIG. 2. Predicted kagome superconducting candidates. (a) Estimated Tc versus electron-phonon-coupling constant λ, with the N(EF) used as the color scale; representative ambient-pressure kagome materials are shown as references [40, 43, 48–56]. (b–f) Phonon dispersions projected by the mode-resolved EPC λνq, together with phonon density of states, Eliashberg spectral function α2F(ω), and accumulated λ(ω) for representative systems: (b) NbBi (P6/mmm), (c) Zn3Al (P63/mmc), (d) Zr3Pb (Pm¯3m), (e) Ti3Si (Pm¯3m), and (f) Zr3Tl2 (R¯3m). λνq denotes the contribution to EPC λ of phonon branch ν at wave vector q.

Fig. 2(a) summarizes the superconducting landscape by plotting the estimated Tc against λ, with N(EF) used as the color scale. The data show the expected broad tendency for Tc to increase with both EPC strength and the Fermi-level den- sity of states, but the spread at fixed λ indicates that phonon- energy scales and mode selectivity are also important. Rep- resentative experimental ambient-pressure kagome supercon- ductors are included in Fig. 2(a) for comparison. The layered reference compounds span different superconducting scales: AV3Sb5 has Tc ≈0.9-2.5 K, CsTi3Bi5 has a reported onset near 4.8 K, and LaRu3Si2 has Tc ≈7 K.
